sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Stripe sells itself as programmable financial infrastructure for any business size, not as a store builder. Each segment page repeats the same frame: one platform, scale from first transaction to enterprise.

facts.text: Home headline frames Stripe as infrastructure across payments, banking and custom revenue models.
facts.quote: from your first transaction to your billionth

facts.text: Startups page targets venture-backed companies with a program and perks.
facts.quote: Designed to support venture-backed businesses that are just getting started.

facts.text: Enterprise page leads with named customers and a volume stat.
facts.quote: Businesses on Stripe generated $1.9 trillion in total volume

gaps: No small-merchant or store-owner landing page appeared in the top-level nav.

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: A 53-product catalogue in eight areas: payments, risk, revenue, data, money management, embedded finance, stablecoins and crypto, and the platform itself. A recommender helps visitors who don't know where to start.

facts.text: The product index lists 53 products.
facts.quote: Showing 53 products.

facts.text: Checkout is the prebuilt payment UI, with a conversion claim.
facts.quote: Launch a secure, customizable, conversion-optimized checkout.

facts.text: Managed Payments is a merchant-of-record offering that takes on tax, fraud and disputes.
facts.quote: Focus on growth while Stripe Managed Payments handles tax, fraud, disputes, and more as your merchant of record.

facts.text: Terminal covers in-person payments with certified hardware.
facts.quote: Accept in-person payments with precertified devices and unified reporting across online and in-person sales.

facts.text: Capital offers loans and merchant cash advances, repaid as a share of daily sales.
facts.quote: Apply for business loans and merchant cash advances in minutes, with no impact to your personal credit score.

facts.text: Connect is the platform and marketplace product; Shopify and DoorDash are named as users.
facts.quote: The world’s most successful platforms and marketplaces, including Shopify and DoorDash, use Stripe Connect to embed payments into their products.

facts.text: Billing covers subscriptions, usage-based billing and invoicing.
facts.quote: One platform to price, meter, bill, invoice, and grow.

gaps: Pricing for Billing, Tax, Radar and Connect was not on the pricing page text captured; only payments, disputes, Terminal and Managed Payments were.

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: Pay-as-you-go with published per-transaction rates and a separate fee list; a 'Custom' tier for volume. Add-ons carry their own monthly or per-event fees.

facts.text: Standard card rate.
facts.quote: 2.9% + 30¢ per successful transaction for domestic cards

facts.text: Standard pricing has no monthly or setup fee, by Stripe's statement.
facts.quote: No setup fees, monthly fees, or hidden fees.

facts.text: Custom pricing is for large volume or unusual models and goes through sales.
facts.quote: Design a custom package— available for businesses with large payments volume or unique business models.

facts.text: Buy-now-pay-later is priced above cards.
facts.quote: 5.99% + 30¢ per successful transaction for Klarna

facts.text: Managed Payments (merchant of record) adds 3.5% on top of payments fees.
facts.quote: 3.5% per successful Managed Payments transaction in addition to Payments fees

facts.text: In-person card rate is lower than online.
facts.quote: 2.7% + 5¢ per successful transaction for domestic cards

facts.text: Each dispute costs $15 to receive.
facts.quote: $15.00 for each dispute you receive.

facts.text: AI-prepared dispute evidence is priced as a share of won disputes.
facts.quote: 30% of the disputed amount for each dispute you win.

facts.text: Card reader hardware starts at $59.
facts.quote: $59.00 Stripe Reader M2

facts.text: Stablecoin payments are 1.5%.
facts.quote: 1.5% of the transaction amount in USD

gaps: No single all-in monthly estimate; the visitor adds fees across products themselves.
IC+ pricing is mentioned but no IC+ rates are shown.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: The strongest part of the site. A public REST API reference with sandboxes, date-and-name versioned releases, SDKs, a CLI, an app and extension model, and AI-agent tooling, all readable logged out.

facts.text: REST, JSON, standard HTTP verbs.
facts.quote: The Stripe API is organized around REST.

facts.text: Official client libraries in seven languages.
facts.quote: Ruby Python PHP Java Node.js Go .NET

facts.text: A stated limit: one object per request.
facts.quote: The Stripe API doesn’t support bulk updates.

facts.text: Sandboxes exist for testing without touching live data.
facts.quote: You can use the Stripe API in sandboxes without affecting your live data or interacting with banking networks.

facts.text: Public changelog with dated, named API versions.
Docs list agent tooling alongside classic dev tools.
facts.quote: Model Context Protocol

facts.text: Docs list an extension model: apps, extensions and custom objects.
facts.quote: Custom objects

gaps: Rate limits, webhooks reliability and SLAs were not read.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: A mission-led narrative: improve conditions for economic growth. Proof is customer outcomes with named brands and large aggregate numbers. The volume figures are phrased differently from page to page.

facts.text: Mission statement.
facts.quote: We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale.

facts.text: Scale claim on About.
facts.quote: More than 5 million businesses build on Stripe

facts.text: Share-of-GDP framing on About.
facts.quote: They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.8% of global GDP.

facts.text: The customers page puts volume lower than the About page does.
facts.quote: we process hundreds of billions of dollars each year for every size of business

facts.text: Customer proof is outcome-led, with named brands.
facts.quote: uplift in Twilio’s payment acceptance rate

gaps: No leadership or investor information in the surveyed pages.

jtbd_fit.evidence: Home names the jobs (accept payments, business banking, custom revenue models); Startups, Enterprise and Platforms pages each name a segment job.

capability_visible.evidence: Public API reference, changelog and product index with in-page UI demos are all readable logged out. The account dashboard sits behind signup.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Standard card, in-person, dispute, hardware and Managed Payments rates are published. Billing, Tax and IC+ rates are not on the captured text.

product_breadth.evidence: 53 products grouped into eight areas, with a recommender for the lost visitor. Many product names are jargon (Authorization Boost, Data Pipeline).

platform_depth.evidence: REST reference, seven SDK languages, sandboxes, named versions, CLI, apps and extensions, MCP and agent skills are all public.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops at the account form; first-payment time was not observed.

friction.evidence: One click from home to the form. Form asks email, full name, password and country, with Google as an alternative.

trust.evidence: Named customers (Twilio, Atlassian, Intercom, Shopify, DoorDash) with specific outcomes. Uptime claim is unsourced.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: Clear to developers and finance leads. 'Financial infrastructure' does not tell a first-time store owner what to do.

proof_quality.evidence: Case stats are named and specific, but the headline GDP ticker has no source and payment-method counts differ by page (100+, 125+, 75+).

persuasion_integrity.evidence: No countdowns or scarcity. A promo rate is labelled with an end date.

cta_logic.evidence: 'Get started' is primary with 'Sign up with Google' and 'Contact sales' ranked below it; pricing page repeats the pattern per tier.

company_narrative.evidence: Same infrastructure story from home to About to Enterprise. Volume is stated as 'trillions' on About but 'hundreds of billions' on Customers.

read.summary: A developer-grade platform with unusually open docs and a published rate card, sold to a broad audience with one infrastructure story. It under-serves the small merchant who lands on the homepage.
pros: Pricing is public and specific, down to dispute and hardware fees.
The API reference, changelog and tooling are readable without an account.
Named customers carry specific outcome numbers.
Signup is one click and one short form from home.
cons: A 53-product catalogue with insider names is hard to navigate for a newcomer.
The homepage GDP ticker and the payment-method counts (100+, 125+, 75+) are not reconciled or sourced.
No all-in cost view; the visitor adds fees across add-ons.
Nothing in the nav speaks to a small store owner.
read.howItSells: Sells credibility and scale: infrastructure language, a very large numbers frame, and named enterprise logos. Then widens by segment (startups, enterprise, platforms) with a program or sales contact for each.
copy: Publish the rate card including the awkward fees.
Keep the API reference and changelog public.
Pair every primary CTA with a sales route for large buyers.
avoid: A live stat with no source.
Different headline counts for the same capability on different pages.
unknowns: What happens after account creation and how long to a first payment.
Billing, Tax, Radar and Connect prices.
Whether the 53-product index helps or overwhelms a real first-time visitor.

hypothesis.statement: A small-merchant path from the homepage (a 'Take your first payment today' card leading to Payment Links) will raise signup completion among non-developer visitors.
hypothesis.metric: Signup-start to account-created rate for non-developer traffic
hypothesis.guardrail: Developer-segment signup rate and sales-contact volume
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship to the segment if completion rises by a pre-agreed margin over two weeks and the developer rate holds.

claims.text: Businesses see 2x growth in payment volume on average.
No setup fees, monthly fees, or hidden fees.
More than 5 million businesses build on Stripe
Intercom takes only 3 months to implement usage-based billing with Stripe.
Pay one flat fee that never changes. There are no compounding interest charges, or late fees.
hundreds of billions of dollars each year
